principles: Soft-retire, never delete. A retired row stays in the DB: it is the audit trail, and 'X MW of announced pipeline died in 2026' is itself market intelligence.
Every status change carries evidence. A transition with no evidence is not applied.
Absence is not death. A project missing from a feed may have been renamed, re-scoped, or the feed may have broken. Only an explicit positive signal retires anything.
No signal derived from private-tier data may drive a published status change.
Every detector answers 'how would we know THIS detector broke' — B8. A detector with no liveness invariant is not deployed.

retirement.effect: retired rows leave SUPPLY calculations but stay in the DB and in the transition log

signals.label: Company terminated or closed in the national register
signals.rationale: An explicit terminated/closed date on the SPV is primary-source evidence that the vehicle is gone. Requires the rename guard: a name that merely disappeared is NOT this signal.

meta_monitor.how_we_know_it_broke: The register parse yields an implausible entity count, or the terminated-share leaves its expected band. A parse bug once marked ALL 486,509 entities terminated because whitespace-only cells read as truthy — that must fail loudly, not retire the fleet.

signals.label: SPV no longer resolvable in the register
signals.rationale: Absence has at least three causes — rename, restructure, broken parse — and only one of them is death. Never retires; flags for a human.

meta_monitor.how_we_know_it_broke: A sudden spike in absent rows across many projects at once indicates a parse or download failure, not a wave of liquidations. Absence affecting more than the spike threshold in one run suppresses the signal and alerts instead.

signals.label: VERT permit valid_until passed with no generation-permit succession
signals.rationale: An expired development permit is a strong but not conclusive death signal — succession may simply not be published yet. Flags; a second consecutive month expired escalates.

meta_monitor.how_we_know_it_broke: The monthly VERT parse produces zero permits, or zero permits carrying a valid_until date. Either means the parser broke rather than that no permits exist.

signals.label: Project vanished from the TSO connection queue between snapshots
signals.rationale: Queue publications are reformatted, re-scoped and re-keyed often. A disappearance is a question, never an answer.

meta_monitor.how_we_know_it_broke: The new snapshot is empty or drastically smaller than the previous one — that is a fetch/parse failure presenting as mass disappearance. The diff is suppressed and an alert fires instead of retiring every project at once.

signals.label: Press signal indicating cancellation or insolvency
signals.rationale: Alert-not-ingest per rule #3. Press is corroboration, never a primary status source.

meta_monitor.how_we_know_it_broke: The tripwire returns zero items for consecutive runs — indistinguishable from a quiet news week unless tracked, so a never-had-items state is reported as BLIND, not as silence.

signals.label: No evidence refresh within the staleness window
signals.rationale: A dossier nobody has re-verified in months is not evidence of death — it is evidence that we stopped looking. Surfaces as a review flag so coverage decay is visible.

meta_monitor.how_we_know_it_broke: This detector cannot go blind — it is computed from stored timestamps. If EVERY row flags stale at once, the intake stopped running, which is itself the alert.

signals.label: Registry/permit sweep found a storage-relevant entity we do not track
signals.rationale: Inflow, not decay. Alert-not-ingest: a discovered entity enters the review queue with its citation, never the public fleet directly (rule #3).

meta_monitor.how_we_know_it_broke: The sweep returns zero candidates across consecutive runs while the register itself grew — that mismatch means the matcher broke, not that Latvia stopped incorporating companies.

rename_check.description: Before any decay signal is allowed to act on a missing or terminated entity, the former-name history is consulted. If the name resolves as a FORMER name whose regcode is still active, the project renamed and the signal is cancelled.
rename_check.records: rename transition with old and new name

digest.rationale: The digest carries detector health in the same message as the findings, so a week of silence from a broken detector cannot read as a quiet week.
